layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We present the DeepGlobe 2018 Satellite Image Under-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: standing Challenge, which includes three public competi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions for segmentation, detection, and classification tasks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on satellite images (Figure 1). Similar to other chal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lenges in computer vision domain such as DAVIS[21] and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: COCO[33], DeepGlobe proposes three datasets and corre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sponding evaluation methodologies, coherently bundled in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: three competitions with a dedicated workshop co-located

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with CVPR 2018.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We observed that satellite imagery is a rich and struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tured source of information, yet it is less investigated than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: everyday images by computer vision researchers. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bridging modern computer vision with remote sensing data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analysis could have critical impact to the way we under-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stand our environment and lead to major breakthroughs in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: global urban planning or climate change research. Keep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing such bridging objective in mind, DeepGlobe aims to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bring together researchers from different domains to raise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: awareness of remote sensing in the computer vision com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: munity and vice-versa. We aim to improve and evaluate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state-of-the-art satellite image understanding approaches,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which can hopefully serve as reference benchmarks for fu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture research in the same topic. In this paper, we analyze

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characteristics of each dataset, define the evaluation crite-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ria of the competitions, and provide baselines for each task.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As machine learning methods dominate the computer vi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion field, public datasets and benchmarks have started to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: play an important role for relative scalability and reliabil-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ity of different approaches. Driven by community efforts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such as ImageNet [45] for object detection, COCO [33] for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image captioning, and DAVIS [21] for object segmentation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computer vision research had been able to push the limits of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: what we can achieve, by using the same annotated datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and common training/validation conventions. Such datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and corresponding challenges increase the visibility, avail-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ability, and feasibility of machine learning models, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: brought up even more scalable, diverse, and accurate algo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rithms to be evaluated on public benchmarks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We observe that satellite imagery is a powerful source of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information as it contains more structured and uniform data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compared to traditional images. Although computer vision

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: community has been accomplishing hard tasks on everyday

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image datasets using deep learning and in contrast to pub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lic datasets released for everyday media, satellite images are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only recently gaining attention from the community for map

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composition, population analysis, effective precision agri-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: culture, and autonomous driving tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To direct more attention to such approaches, we present

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DeepGlobe 2018, a Satellite Image Understanding Chal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lenge, which (i) contains three datasets structured to solve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: three different satellite image understanding tasks, (ii) orga-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nizes three public challenges to propose solutions to these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks, and (iii) gathers researchers from diverse fields to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unite all expertises to solve similar tasks in a collaborative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: workshop. The datasets created and released for this com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: petition may serve as (iv) fair and durable reference bench-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: marks for future research in satellite image analysis. Fur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thermore, since the challenge tasks involve “in the wild"

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forms of classic computer vision problems (e.g., image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: classification, detection, and semantic segmentation), these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets have the potential to become valuable testbeds for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the design of robust vision algorithms, beyond the area of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: remote sensing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The three tracks for DeepGlobe are defined as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Road Extraction Challenge: In disaster zones, espe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cially in developing countries, maps and accessibility

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information are crucial for crisis response. We pose the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenge of automatically extracting roads and street

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: networks remotely from satellite images as a first step

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for automated crisis response and increased map cov-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erage for connectivity.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Building Detection Challenge: As evidenced by re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cent catastrophic natural events, modeling population

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dynamics is of great importance for disaster response

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and recovery. Thus, modeling urban demographics is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a vital task and detection of buildings and urban areas

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are key to achieve it. We pose the challenge of au-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tomatically detecting buildings from satellite images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for gathering aggregate urban information remotely as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well as for gathering detailed information about spatial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distribution of urban settlements.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Land Cover Classification Challenge: Automatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: categorization and segmentation of land cover is es-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sential for sustainable development, agriculture [11],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forestry [17, 16] and urban planning [20]. Therefore

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we pose the challenge of classifying land types from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satellite images for economic and agricultural automa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion solutions, among the three topics of DeepGlobe,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: probably as the most studied one in the intersection of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: remote sensing and image processing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We currently host three public competitions based on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks of extracting roads, detecting buildings, and classify-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing land cover types in the satellite images. The combined

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets include over 10K satellite images. Section 2 ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plains the characteristics of images, details the annotation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process, and introduces the division of training, validation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and test sets. Section 3 describes the tasks in detail and pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poses the evaluation metric used for each task. Section 4

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provides an overview of the current approaches and gives

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our preliminary baselines for the competitions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results of the competitions will be presented in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DeepGlobe 2018 Workshop during the 2018 International

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (CVPR) in Salt Lake City, Utah on June 18th, 2018. As of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: May 15st, 2018, more than 950 participants have registered

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in DeepGlobe competitions and there are more than 90 valid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: submissions in the leaderboard over the three tracks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this Section, we will discuss the dataset and imagery

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characteristics for each DeepGlobe track, followed by an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explanation of the methodology for the annotation process

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to obtain the training labels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1. Road Extraction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: There have been several datasets proposed in the liter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ature for benchmarking algorithms for semantic segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of overhead imagery. Some of these can be enumer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ated as the TorontoCity[54] dataset, the ISPRS 2D semantic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labeling dataset [3], the Mnih dataset [39], the SpaceNet

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset [2] and the ISPRS Benchmark for Multi-Platform

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Photogrammetry [4].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The satellite imagery used in DeepGlobe for the road ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: traction challenge is sampled from the DigitalGlobe +Vivid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Images dataset [1]. It covers images captured over Thai-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: land, Indonesia, and India. The ground resolution of the im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: age pixels is 50 cm/pixel. The images consist of 3 channels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Red, Green and Blue). Each of the original geotiff images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are 19'584 × 19'584 pixels. The annotation process starts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by tiling and loading these images in QGIS[7]. Based on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this tiling, we determine useful areas to sample from those

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: countries. For designating useful areas, we sample data uni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formly between rural and urban areas. After sampling we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: select the corresponding DigitalGlobe tiff images belong-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing to those areas. These images are then cropped to extract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: useful subregions and relevant subregions are sampled by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: GIS experts. (A useful subregion denotes a part of the im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: age where we have a good relative ratio between positive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and negative examples.) Also, while selecting these sub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: regions, we try to sample interesting areas uniformly, e.g.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: those with different types of road surfaces (unpaved, paved,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dirt roads), rural and urban areas, etc. An example of one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image crop is illustrated in the left panel of Figure 1. It is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 2: Road labels are annotated on top of the satellite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image patches, all taken from DeepGlobe Road Extraction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Challenge dataset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: important to note that the labels generated are pixel-based,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where all pixels belonging to the road are labeled, instead

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of labeling only the centerline.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The final road dataset consists of a total of 8'570 im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages and spans a total land area of 2'220km2. Of those,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6′226 images (72.7% of the dataset), spanning a total of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1′632km2, were split as the training dataset. 1′243 images,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spanning 362km2, were chosen as the validation dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 1'101 images were chosen for testing which cover a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: total land area of 288km2. The split of the dataset to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training/validation/testing subsets is conducted by random-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: izing among tiles to aim for an approximate distribution of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 70%/15%/15%. The training dataset consists of4.5% pos-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: itive and 95.5% negative pixels, the validation dataset con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sists of 3% positive and 97% negative pixels and the test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset consists of 4.1% positive and 95.9% negative pix-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: els. We selected a diverse set of patches to demonstrate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: road labels annotated on the original satellite images in Fig-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ure 2. As shown, the urban morphology, the illumination

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions, the road density, and the structure of the street

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: networks are significantly diverse among the samples.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.2. Building Detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DeepGlobe Building Detection Challenge uses the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SpaceNet Building Detection Dataset. Previous compe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: titions on building extraction using satellite data, PRRS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2008 [10] and ISPRS [3, 5], were based on small areas (a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: few km2) and in some cases used a combination of opti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cal data and LiDAR data. The Inria Aerial Image Labeling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: covered 810km² area with 30cm resolution in various Eu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ropean and American cities [35]. It addressed model porta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bility between areas as some cities were included only in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training data and some only in testing data. SpaceNet was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the first challenge that involved large areas including cities

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Asia and Africa.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The dataset includes four areas: Las Vegas, Paris, Shang-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hai, and Khartoum. The labeled dataset consists of 24'586

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 200m × 200m (corresponding to 650 × 650 pixels) non-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: overlapping scenes containing a total of 302'701 building

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: footprints across all areas. The areas are of urban and sub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: urban nature. The source imagery is from the WorldView-3

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sensor, which has both a 31cm single-band panchromatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a 1.24m multi-spectral sensor providing 8-band multi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spectral imagery with 11-bit radiometric resolution. A GIS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: team at DigitalGlobe (now Radiant Solutions) fully anno-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tated each scene, identifying and providing a polygon foot-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: print for each building to the published specification, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were extracted to best represent the building footprint (see

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the central panel of Figure 1 for an example). Any par-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tially visible rooftops were approximated to represent the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shape of the building. Adjoining buildings were marked

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as a single building. The dataset was split 60%/20%/20%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for train/validation/test. As per the nature of human-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: building annotation, some small errors are inevitable espe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cially for rural areas. We leave the analysis of annotater

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disagreement for future work.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Each area is covered by a single satellite image, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constitutes an easier problem to solve compared to data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where different parts are covered by images having different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sun and satellite angles, and different atmospheric condi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions. Atmospheric compensation process can process im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages to create data that reflects surface reflectance there-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fore reducing effects of atmosphere, but different shadow

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lengths and different satellite orientation can possibly cre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ate problems for detection algorithms if models are used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to classify images acquired at different time with different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sun/satellite angles.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The SpaceNet data[9] is distributed under a Creative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and is hosted as a public dataset on Amazon Web Services

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and can be downloaded for free.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.3. Land Cover Classification

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Semantic segmentation started to attract more research

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: activities as a challenging task. The ISPRS Vaihingen and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Potsdam [3] and the Zeebruges data [22] are popular public

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets for this task. The ISPRS Vaihingen dataset con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixels), with 16 fully annotated images. ISPRS Potsdam

layout_dets.text: cluding SWIR) WorldView-3 images. Besides urban areas,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: another important application of land cover classification is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: humanitarian studies focusing more on rural areas at mid-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution (~ 30m/pixel). For similar problems Landsat

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data is (i.e., crop type classification[31]). Still, the low res-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: olution of Landsat data limits the information it can provide.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The DeepGlobe Land Cover Classification Challenge is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the first public dataset offering high-resolution sub-meter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satellite imagery focusing on rural areas. Due to the variety

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of land cover types and to the density of annotations, this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset is more challenging than existing counterparts de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scribed above. DeepGlobe Land Cover Classification Chal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lenge dataset contains 1′146 satellite images of size 2′448 ×

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2'448 pixels in total, split into training/validation/test sets,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each with 803/171/172 images (corresponding to a split of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 70%/15%/15%). All images contain RGB data, with a pixel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution of 50 cm, collected from the DigitalGlobe Vivid+

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset as described in Section 2.1. The total area size of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset is equivalent to 1'716.9km².

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Each satellite image is paired with a mask image for land

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cover annotation. The mask is an RGB image with 7 classes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: following the Anderson Classification [14]. The class dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tributions are available in Table 1.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Urban land: Man-made, built up areas with human ar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tifacts.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Agriculture land: Farms, any planned (i.e. regular)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plantation, cropland, orchards, vineyards, nurseries,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and ornamental horticultural areas; confined feeding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corresponding original image (left) pairs from interesting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: areas. Label colors are given in Table 1.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Rangeland: Any non-forest, non-farm, green land,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grass.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Forest land: Any land with at least 20% tree crown

layout_dets.text: density plus clear cuts.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Water: Rivers, oceans, lakes, wetland, ponds.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Barren land: Mountain, rock, dessert, beach, land with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Unknown: Clouds and others.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The annotations are pixel-wise segmentation masks cre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ated by professional annotators (see the right hand panel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Figure 1). The images in the dataset were sampled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from full-size tiles to assure that all land cover classes have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enough representation. In our specifications, we indicated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that any instance of a class larger than a roughly 20m × 20m

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: would be annotated. However, land cover pixel-wise clas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sification from high-resolution satellite imagery is still an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exploratory task, and some small human error is inevitable.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In addition, we intentionally did not annotate roads and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bridges because it is already covered in the road extraction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenge. Some example labeled areas are demonstrated in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 3 as examples of farm, forest, and urban dominant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tiles, and a mixed tile.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Tasks and Evaluations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this section, we formally define the expected task in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each challenge and explain the evaluation metrics used in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: terms of their computation and implementation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1. Road Extraction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We formulate the task of road extraction from satellite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images as a binary classification problem. Each input is a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satellite image. The solution is expected to predict a mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the input (i.e., a binary image of the same height and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: width as the input with road and non-road pixel labels).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: There have been previous challenges on road mask ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: traction, e.g., the SpaceNet [2]. Their metric was based on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Averaged Path Length Similarity (APLS) metric [51]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that measures distance between ground truth road network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: represented in vector form with a solution graph also in vec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tor form. Any proposed road graph G with missing edges

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., if an overhanging tree is inferred to sever a road) is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: penalized by the APLS metric, so ensuring that roads are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properly connected is crucial for a high score.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In our case, we use the pixel-wise Intersection over

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Union (IoU) score as our evaluation metric for each image,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: defined as Eqn. (1).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is the number of pixels that are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wrongly predicted as road pixel, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is the number

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of pixels that are wrongly predicted as non-road pixel for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image i. Assuming there are n images, the final score is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: defined as the average IoU among all images (Eqn. (2)).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2. Building Detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In DeepGlobe, building detection is based on a binary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation task, where the input is a satellite image and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the output is a list of building polygons. Multiple perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance measures can be applied to score participants. PRRS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2008 [10] challenge used 8 different performance measures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our evaluation metric for this competition is an F1 score

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the matching algorithm inspired by Algorithm 2 in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ILSVRC paper applied to the detection of building foot-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prints [45]. This metric was decided to emphasize the im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: portance of both accurate detection of buildings and the im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: portance of complete identification of building outlines in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an area. Buildings with a pixel area of 20 pixels or less

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were discarded, as these small buildings are artifacts of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image tiling process when a tile boundary cuts a building

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into multiple parts.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A detected building is scored as a true positive if the IoU

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Eqn.3) between the ground truth (GT) building area A and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the detected building area B is larger than 0.5. If a proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: building intersects with multiple GT buildings, then the GT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: building with the largest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: value will be selected.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The solution score is defined by F1 measure (Eqn. 4),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is number of true positives, M is the number

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of ground truth buildings and N is the number of detected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: buildings.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The implementation and detailed description of scoring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be found in the SpaceNet Utilities GitHub repo [9]. We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: score each area separately and the final score is the average

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of scores for each area as in Eqn. 5.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.3. Land Cover Classification

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The land cover classification problem is defined as a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multi-class segmentation task to detect areas of classes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentioned in Section 2.3. The evaluation is computed based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the accuracy of the class labels and averages over classes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are considered. The class unknown' is removed from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluation, as it does not correspond to a land cover class,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but rather to the presence of clouds.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Each input is a satellite image. The solution is expected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to predict an RGB mask for the input, i.e., a colored image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the same height and width as the input image. The ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pected result is a land cover map of same size in pixels as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the input image, where the color of each pixel indicates its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: class label.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: There have been previous challenges on road mask ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: traction (e.g., the TiSeLaC [8]), which emphasized the us-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: age of temporal information of the dataset. Our challenge,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the other hand, uses images captured at one timestamp

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as the input, thus more flexible in real applications. Other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: previous land cover / land use semantic segmentation chal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lenges as the ISPRS [3] or the IEEE GRSS data fusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contests [22, 57] also used single shot ground truths and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reported overall and average accuracy scores as evaluation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metrics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Similar to the road extraction challenge, we use the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel-wise Intersection over Union (IoU) score as our eval-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uation metric. It was defined slightly differently for each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: class, as there are multiple categories (Eqn. 6). Assuming

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: there are n images, the formulation is defined as,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rectly predicted as class

layout_dets.text: is the number of pixels in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image i that are wrongly predicted as class

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the number of pixels in image i that are wrongly predicted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as any class other than class

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Note that we have an un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: known class that is not active in our evaluation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predictions on such pixels will not be added to the calcula-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion and thus do not affect the final score). Assuming there

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are k land cover classes, the final score is defined as the

layout_dets.text: average IoU among all classes as in Eqn. (7).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. State-of-the-art and Baselines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The tasks defined in the previous section have been ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plored in different datasets with different methods, some of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which are also shared publicly. In this section we will intro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duce the state of the art approaches for each task compar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing their dataset to DeepGlobe. As a baseline, we will also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: share our preliminary results based on current approaches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on each dataset, which sets the expected success figures for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the challenge participants as well as guide them to develop

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: novel approaches.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.1. Road Extraction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Automating the generation of road networks is exten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sively studied in the computer vision and computer graph-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ics world. The procedural generation of streets [13, 23]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creates detailed and structurally realistic models, however

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: written grammars are not based on the real world. On

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the other hand, some inverse procedural modeling (IPM)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approaches [12] process real-world data (images, LiDAR,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: etc.) to extract realistic representations. Following the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example-based generation idea, another approach is to use

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: already existing data resources, such as aerial images [37,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 38], or geostationary satellite images [26, 58]. Similar

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approaches extract road networks using neural networks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for dynamic environments [53] from LiDAR data [59],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using line integrals [32] and using image processing ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proaches [43, 55].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Similar to the experiments of [26] and [37], we explored

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our baseline approach to follow some state-of-the-art deep

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning models [19, 24, 28, 44]. In contrast to those ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proaches, our dataset is more diverse, spanning three coun-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tries with significant changes in topology and climate; and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significantly larger in area and size. The best results were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: obtained by training a modified version of DeepLab [24] ar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chitecture with ResNet18 backbone and Focal Loss [49]. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: order to provide a baseline to evaluate the network, we only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: added simple rotation as data augmentation, and we did not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: apply any post-processing to the results, only binarizing all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results at a fixed threshold of 128. With this setup, we ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tained an IoU score of 0.545 after training 100 epochs. Two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example results are given in Figure 4, showing the satellite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image, extracted road mask, and ground truth road mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from left to right. The vanishing roads suggest that post-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processing techniques other than simple thresholding would

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yield more connected roads.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.2. Building Detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Building detection and building footprint segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has been subject of research for long time. Early work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was based on pan-sharpened images and was using land

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cover classification to find vegetation, shadows, water and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: man-made areas followed by segmentation and classifica-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 4: Example results of our road extraction method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with an IoU score of 0.545, with satellite image (left), ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tracted road mask (middle), and the ground truth (right).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of segments into building/non-building areas [10]. Re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: searchers sometimes transformed pixels into HSV color

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: space, which alleviates effects of different illumination on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitched roofs. In [41] the author used shadow information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and vegetation/shadow/man-made classification combined

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with graph approach to detect buildings.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mnih [40] used two locally connected NN layers fol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowed by a fully connected layer. He also took into account

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: omission noise (some objects are not marked in the ground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: truth data) by modifying loss function and mis-registration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: noise (such noise exists if the ground truth is not based on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image, but on some other data, such as OSM [6] or survey

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data) by allowing for translational noise. Vakalopoulou et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: al. [50] used convolutional layers of AlexNet to extract fea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures that were used as input to SVM classifier which was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 4.3. Land Cover Classification

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Land Cover Classification from satellite imagery is a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: very active research problem in remote sensing. Earlier

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work mostly focus on image classification, where each im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: age is only classified to one label. Yang and Newsam[56]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used Bag-of-Visual-Words and SVM to classify a dataset of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2′100 images containing 21 classes each with 100 images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of size 256 × 256 pixels. The best accuracy reported[56]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was 81.19%, and the data was released as UC Merced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset[56], which later became a popular dataset for land

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cover image classification. Scott et al.[48] applied DCNN-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based approach on the UCM dataset and obtained a best

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accuracy of 98.5% with ResNet-50.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Compared to image-level classification problem, pixel-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wise classification, or semantic segmentation, started to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attract more research activities as a challenging task, for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which deep learning pipelines are becoming the state of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the art [60]. Volpi and Tuia [52] proposed to use an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: downsample-upsample CNN-based architecture and ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tained an F1 score of 83.58% on Vaihingen and 87.97%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on Potsdam. Audebert et al. [18] trained a variant of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SegNet architecture with multi-kernel convolutional layer,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and achieved 89.8% on Vaihingen. Marmanis and col-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leagues [36] achieved similar performances using an en-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semble of CNNs models trained to recognized classes and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using edges information between classes. Authors in [22]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 5. Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We introduced the DeepGlobe Satellite Image Under-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: standing Challenge. DeepGlobe 2018 provides datasets,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenges, and a CVPR 2018 workshop structured around

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the three tasks of understanding roads, buildings, and land

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cover types from satellite images. In this paper, we analyzed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the datasets and explained the evaluation metrics for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: public challenges. We also provided some baselines com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pared to the state-of-the-art approaches. Based on the cur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rent feedback, we believe that the DeepGlobe datasets will

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: become valuable benchmarks in satellite image understand-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing, enabling more collaborative interdisciplinary research

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the area, that can be fairly compared and contrasted us-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing our benchmark, leading to new exciting developments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at the intersection of computer vision, machine learning, re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mote sensing, and geosciences.
